title: colonnade-headline — stacked word column beside a tall portrait plate
idea: The headline is broken one word per line down the left edge, each word sitting on its own baseline in a narrow vertical column, and directly beside it a tall portrait-format photograph rises the full height of the band like a second column. The visitor reads down the words the way they read down the picture, so the copy and the image behave as two parallel vertical shafts rather than a block of text with an illustration attached. It is for a hero that wants the headline to be structural — architecture, not banner.
why_new: It is not foreground-split, whose regions are side-by-side blocks of ordinary text and landscape media rather than two vertical shafts of equal height; and it is not vertical-rail, where the rotated wordmark is a decorative spine at the frame edge and the real composition happens in the field beside it. Here the headline is upright, word-stacked, full-height, and is itself one of the two columns.
built_from: An outer Group (constrained, tall min-height) containing a two-column Columns block: the narrow left column holds the H1 Heading plus a short Paragraph and one Buttons block anchored to the bottom; the right column holds a single Image block in portrait ratio. One reviewed CSS hook — a class on the Columns block that sets the band's min-height, forces the heading's word-per-line stacking and tight leading, stretches the image to fill the column height with object-fit, and flips the flex direction to a stacked column below the breakpoint.
risk: A headline longer than four short words turns the left column into a thin ribbon of hyphenated fragments, and any word wider than the column overflows or shrinks the type to nothing — the archetype needs a brief with a genuinely short, punchy H1. It also needs a real portrait-orientation photograph; a landscape crop letterboxed into the tall column immediately looks like a placeholder and the whole composition reads as a broken two-column layout rather than an authored one.
